content_units: Best Prepaid Fit for a Nairobi Remote Worker

For a remote worker in Nairobi using heavy data, café Wi‑Fi backup, frequent video calls, and occasional international calling,   Plan B is the best overall value under KES 2,300  . It gives the strongest balance of   high-speed data headroom + included international minutes   without adding a major price jump.
Plan Comparison for Heavy Remote Work
Plan   Monthly Price   High-Speed Data   Local Minutes   International Calling   Key Limitation
A   KES 1,500   20 GB then throttled   500   Billed separately   Lowest data buffer; extra intl cost
B   KES 2,200   40 GB   300   60 min included   Fewer local minutes than A/C
C   KES 1,900   25 GB   Unlimited   20 min included   Hotspot capped at 10 GB
Option 1:   Plan B     Best balance for video calls, tethering flexibility, and occasional international calls     40 GB + 60 intl min
Choose B
Option 2:   Plan C     Good mid-price option if you need unlimited local calls and only light hotspot use     KES 300 cheaper than B
Consider C
Option 3:   Plan A     Cheapest upfront, but weakest fit for heavy work data and international calling     Lowest monthly cost
Budget Pick
Why Plan B Wins for Your Use Case
-   40 GB is the key advantage.   Video meetings can burn through data quickly, especially with 3 café workdays per week and mobile backup usage. Plan B gives much more breathing room than A or C.
-   60 international minutes included   is a strong value add. Since your international calling is occasional, this likely covers your needs without unpredictable top-up charges.
-   Under your budget ceiling.   At   KES 2,200  , it stays within the   KES 2,300   limit while delivering the best remote-work readiness.
-   Better risk protection than Plan A.   Plan A looks cheaper, but 20 GB high-speed can run out fast, and throttling during work calls or hotspot use is a real productivity hit.

-   More flexible than Plan C.   C has unlimited local minutes, but remote work quality depends more on data than voice minutes, and the   10 GB hotspot cap   can become frustrating if café Wi‑Fi is unreliable.
Best-Value Recommendation
Recommended: Plan B
Why:
- Highest usable high-speed data for work
- Includes enough international minutes to avoid extra billing stress
- Still within budget
- Best suited to video calls, cloud work, and backup tethering
When Plan C would be better instead:
Choose C only if you make lots of local calls and rarely use hotspot data.

Planning Context
Using typical remote-work behavior, I prioritized:
- high-speed data before throttling
- included international minutes
- reliability for video calls and tethering
- staying under   KES 2,300/month
